title: Arson and blockades across Bangladesh as banned Awami League holds 'lockdown'
dek: Vehicles, homes of MPs and police property were set on fire in at least 10 districts, with the worst violence in Sheikh Hasina's home district of Gopalganj. About 3,000 border guards were deployed.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Activists of Bangladesh's banned Awami League set fire to vehicles, homes and offices and blocked highways and railway lines in at least 10 districts on Thursday during a dawn-to-dusk "lockdown" called by the party, according to reports, as the government deployed about 3,000 border guards to help the police and moved to extend the deployment across the country from Friday, according to reports.

The worst violence was in Gopalganj, the home district of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, south-west of Dhaka and the part of Bangladesh closest to West Bengal. No deaths were reported on Thursday itself, but at least four people were killed in violence in the two days before the lockdown, according to reports.

## What happened

In Gopalganj, attackers threw a crude bomb at the house of Selimuzzaman Selim, the member of parliament for Gopalganj-1, at about 10.30 am, then poured petrol on it and set it alight, according to reports. Reports differ on the number of vehicles set on fire at Muksudpur police station, putting it at about 15 or at least 20. The homes of Gopalganj-2 MP KM Babar and a former district BNP president were also attacked, as was a Grameen Bank branch. Rail services through the district were suspended. "The station's operations are currently suspended," a police officer told reporters.

In Dhaka, a crude bomb went off beneath the Agargaon metro station at about 12.10 pm, injuring no one, and masked men set fire to the car of Mojibur Rahman Monju, chairman of the AB Party, outside its office before dawn, according to reports. Buses were burned in Sylhet, Rajshahi and Narayanganj, and the homes of several former Awami League ministers were attacked or set on fire in Rajshahi, Barishal and Patuakhali. Activists blocked the Dhaka-Khulna and Dhaka-Barishal highways with felled trees and burning tyres, cutting road links to about 21 south-western districts, and several trains were cancelled or cut short.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police said it had arrested 565 people in the 24 hours before the lockdown, including 71 leaders and activists of the Awami League and its student wing, among them former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, according to reports.

## Security response

The home ministry ordered 96 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), nearly 3,000 personnel, into seven districts: Dhaka, Chattogram, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Mymensingh and Faridpur. Reports differ on how many went to Gopalganj, from 21 to 27 platoons. The Civil Aviation Authority put all airports on heightened alert, according to reports.

The party's demands include lifting the ban on its activities and cancelling the death sentence passed on Ms Hasina, according to reports. The government has blamed former Awami League leaders living abroad for encouraging the violence; Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told parliament this week that those who attacked police would be identified and "brought under the law".

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

Ms Hasina has lived in India since an uprising drove her from power in August 2024, and has said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December. Dhaka has asked New Delhi to extradite her; India says the request is being examined under established legal procedures. Unrest in Gopalganj, Faridpur and the other south-western districts that border or lie close to West Bengal is watched closely along the border, and any wider crackdown or flight of people would be felt first in Bengal's border districts.

The violence comes as the two countries prepare for a meeting in Dhaka of the joint committee set up under the Ganges Water Treaty from 21 to 23 November, with the Ganges Water Treaty due to expire on 12 December, and as Bangladesh's garment sector faces fresh unrest over wages.

## What happens next

The wider BGB deployment is expected to begin on Friday, according to reports. The Awami League has not said whether it will call further shutdowns.
